description: Build the simulation around symplectic integrators from day one. Use leapfrog as the minimum viable integrator, then compose it into Yoshida 4th-order. This ensures energy conservation is architectural, not a post-hoc fix.
rationale: Energy conservation is the primary correctness signal for any N-body simulation. A non-symplectic integrator (Euler, RK4) will show secular energy drift that compounds over time, making long-term simulations meaningless.

description: Use Structure-of-Arrays (numpy arrays) rather than Array-of-Structs (Python objects). All particle state is flat numpy arrays: pos(N,d), vel(N,d), mass(N). Force computation is vectorized with broadcasting.
rationale: Python object overhead kills performance. Numpy vectorization gives 100x speedup over pure Python loops. This is the single biggest performance decision for a Python-based sim.

description: Implement Barnes-Hut tree as the scaling breakthrough. The concept path 01_newtonian_gravity -> 10_force_decomposition -> 05_barnes_hut_tree -> 09_vectorized_computation provides a natural progression from O(N^2) brute-force to O(N log N) tree code.
rationale: Brute-force O(N^2) is a hard wall at N>1000. Barnes-Hut is the canonical solution and the minimal tree code that demonstrates scaling improvement.
